claim: A selected policy topic determines the paper's country comparison; persistent country-year records expose treated and control before/after changes, and DID subtracts the control change from the treated change.

manuscript_evidence.supports: LDA after text cleaning; six policy themes; criminal-legislation keywords cybercrime/warrant/penalty. Other displayed keyword families are source-listed.
Each theme uses 1-2 treated countries and an equal number of controls with similar internet penetration; no explicit one-to-one matching procedure.

caption: Conceptual policy-evaluation mechanism for cybercrime criminal legislation. Paper-listed policy keywords identify a theme whose reported treated group (Australia and Ireland) and control group (UK and New Zealand) are followed before and after a relative adoption boundary. The register exposes the symbolic difference of within-group changes, with internet-penetration comparability and covariate adjustment shown as supporting study context. Records are schematic; no effect estimate or policy-efficacy conclusion is reproduced.
placement: Focused overview of the policy-evaluation mechanism, suitable before section 5 model details; not an exhaustive summary of all KDMF components.

review.review_type: Actual final-raster visual self-review against the scene-trial source evidence; not an independent review.
checks: Eight country-year records use shared table rules rather than separate floating cards.
Australia/Ireland and UK/New Zealand explicitly identify the treated and control group means.
Each within-group change is post minus pre, and DID is treated change minus control change.
Covariates share one folio and one supporting leader; similar internet penetration remains a selection criterion.
The scene reports the paper’s study groups and symbolic records, not current national law or an estimated effect.
notes: Conceptual scene, not a rerun of the paper’s empirical results.
Source inconsistencies remain in source_notes; no silent numeric reconstruction.
Publication-size typography and physical print proof remain author checks.

approval_evidence.scope: Selected figures 01–04 with requested local corrections and bilingual showcase only; not knowledge-base admission or independent scientific validation.

source_notes.issue: Y is defined as number of cybercrimes; surrounding descriptions repeatedly call the outcome a rate, and result tables call it normalized number of cases.
source_notes.handling: Use Recorded cases and symbolic operands; no rate denominator or empirical scale.

source_notes.issue: Positive treated*time coefficients on normalized case counts are interpreted as reducing cybercrime; the source supplies no outcome recoding that resolves that interpretation.
source_notes.handling: Omit effects, directions, benefit colors and policy efficacy rankings; do not silently correct the signs.

source_notes.issue: Narrative interaction p=0.047 conflicts with table p=0.01. Table 5 repeats most Table 4 values; treated coefficient differs while its t and interval are reused.
source_notes.handling: Record conflict, omit the numerical result and related efficacy claim.

source_notes.locator: p.21 sensitivity text versus pp.16-17 policy themes
source_notes.issue: Fourth group is named Network Operators but baseline beta=0.286 corresponds to Critical Infrastructure; Network Operators earlier uses 0.310. Reported sensitivity p near 0.229 is also inconsistent with the operator table.
source_notes.handling: Do not use sensitivity to claim stable identification or scientific approval.

source_notes.locator: p.9 K-selection prose and p.10 Figure 6
source_notes.issue: Prose says K=2 has highest silhouette score; Figure 6 shows 0.41 at K=2, 0.42 at K=3, and 0.43 at K=4. Source nevertheless chooses K=3.
source_notes.handling: Clustering omitted from focused mechanism; no silhouette justification or cluster-to-treatment edge.

source_notes.locator: p.14 variable definition and p.15 displayed DID equation
source_notes.issue: treated_it is described as implementation status in a country-year, while time_it denotes post period and the model includes their interaction; distinction between fixed group membership and time-varying exposure is ambiguous.
source_notes.handling: Use source-reported Treated in study/Control in study identities plus Before/After and symbolic contrast. No binary design matrix or claim to reproduce fitted coding.

source_notes.issue: CEI is transformed using (1-original CEI)*100 so higher is lower exposure, but the prose later describes effective strategies resulting in low CEI scores.
source_notes.handling: CEI is outside the selected policy scene; no CEI values or directional interpretation drawn.

source_notes.locator: p.1 summary, p.22 section 9.1, p.25 memo
source_notes.issue: Summary and memo describe three submodels, while strengths describe four submodels.
source_notes.handling: Do not force an exhaustive numbered model count or equal modules.

source_notes.issue: NSCI is used for number of cybercrime incidents on p.19, close to NCSI used for preparedness; labels risk conflation.
source_notes.handling: Use unambiguous Y and Recorded cases; the separate factor-regression branch is omitted.

design_revision.summary: Policy text leads to country-year records and the treated/control changes that form a difference-in-differences contrast.

relationship_representation: Semantic model relations; not every relation is a continuous arrow. Repeated labels, equations and shared table alignment also encode correspondence.

style_adaptation.approach: Concrete scientific objects with integrated transformations; selective shared rules instead of repeated equal cards.
